stories.title: Allowing AI firms to collude to ‘pace the frontier’ is a dangerous proposition
stories.simple_summary: Some people are worried that AI companies might be allowed to work together to control how fast AI develops, rather than competing separately. This could give them too much power over the technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly about how government rules should work — it affects what AI tools exist in the future, but there's nothing specific you need to do right now.

stories.title: Gates Foundation commits $1 billion to improving global AI access
stories.simple_summary: Bill Gates is giving $1 billion (a thousand million dollars) to help more people around the world get access to AI tools and technology.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually mean AI becomes more available to small businesses in developing countries, but it's years away from affecting most people.

stories.title: Poll: Americans say there’s a serious risk of AI destroying humanity
stories.simple_summary: A poll asked Americans if they're worried AI could destroy humanity — and many said yes, they think there's a serious risk.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows people are nervous about AI, but polls measure opinions, not actual dangers — it mostly reflects how people feel rather than what will actually happen.

stories.title: Why Trump is all-in on AI despite the warnings
stories.simple_summary: President Trump supports developing AI quickly, even though many experts are warning about risks.
stories.why_it_matters: This shapes which government policies get made, but it's political news — you don't need to change anything unless you work in AI or politics.

stories.title: Bipartisan, big tech push for AI regulation comes as Trump claims 'hoax'
stories.simple_summary: Members from both political parties want to create rules for AI safety, but President Trump says that's unnecessary.
stories.why_it_matters: This is a political debate about future regulations — nothing affects you personally unless you own an AI company.

stories.title: Why the US and China are at odds on AI threats
stories.simple_summary: The United States and China disagree about what dangers AI poses and how to handle them.
stories.why_it_matters: This is about international relations between two countries — it doesn't directly change how AI works for ordinary people.

stories.title: We don’t need AI regulation — leave safety to us, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang says
stories.simple_summary: Nvidia's leader (a big AI hardware company) says companies should handle their own AI safety instead of having government rules.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and people in the tech industry — it's one company's opinion on policy, not something affecting your daily life.

stories.title: AI and data centers are incredibly unpopular in every poll
stories.simple_summary: A poll shows that most Americans (61%) don't want AI data centers built in their areas. Data centers are huge computer warehouses that use lots of electricity to power AI.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live near where a data center might be built, this could matter — communities are pushing back against construction because of noise, power use, and environmental concerns.

stories.title: Trump Defended A.I. Data Centers on Truth Social, and Commenters Clapped Back
stories.simple_summary: President Trump publicly supported building AI data centers, but people responded online disagreeing with him.
stories.why_it_matters: This is political debate online — no immediate change to what you need to do, but it shows communities are concerned about data centers.

stories.title: The AI data center boom is colliding with cities scarred by big industry
stories.simple_summary: AI data centers are being proposed in cities that already have pollution problems from old factories. In Philadelphia, people worry about building another major industrial facility in an area still recovering from a closed oil refinery.
stories.why_it_matters: If you live in or near a city considering a data center, this means the debate about whether to allow it in your community is heating up.

stories.title: Meta now lets AI agents handle the boring parts of WhatsApp Business setup
stories.simple_summary: Meta (which owns WhatsApp) now has AI that can automatically set up WhatsApp Business accounts and handle routine tasks for developers.
stories.why_it_matters: If you run a small business using WhatsApp, setup might eventually become easier, but this is technical news mainly for people building apps — it doesn't affect regular WhatsApp users yet.

stories.title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
stories.simple_summary: The headline lists AI projects and companies that failed or got shut down, showing that not every AI project succeeds.
stories.why_it_matters: This is industry news showing that hype doesn't always match reality — useful to remember before believing every AI announcement, but no specific action needed.
